headline: High-risk git/workspace collision and medium prompt-injection/cascade risks: Aider’s shared repo writes can corrupt or misapply B’s uploads, while B’s outputs can be treated as authoritative without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, so if social-auto-upload places attacker-controlled content in that workspace, Aider may ingest it as trusted text. B has file inputs and broad network egress, but no explicit provenance checks. The pathway exists in default shared-workspace use, though not via a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or mounted workspace
IF B writes content that Aider later opens as task context or instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require manual review of any file B writes before Aider reads it
Use read-only mounts for B’s input directory
Add a provenance prefix to B-generated files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can send context to configured model providers; social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If they share a workspace, Aider can expose B’s files to third-party inference, creating a plausible leakage path. B itself has no filesystem read, so the main risk is Aider’s outbound context handling.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or repo checkout
IF Aider is configured to send file contents from that shared workspace to a model provider
mitigations: Keep account-data files outside Aider’s repo
Redact secrets before Aider opens any B-related files
Use separate OS users for each agent
Disable automatic inclusion of unrelated files in prompts
requires-engineering: add DLP or path allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while social-auto-upload has file inputs and broad network egress. In a shared repo, Aider can rewrite files that B later uploads, and concurrent edits can corrupt git state. The pair’s shared-state model makes this a default collision risk, not a niche configuration issue.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or shared working tree
IF B uploads artifacts that Aider can modify before upload
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate clone
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable auto-commit while B is active
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits that social-auto-upload could consume as files or artifacts, while B has network egress to external services. If B treats Aider’s output as authoritative, an error in Aider can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the unsafe path is plausible by default.
conditions: IF B ingests files or artifacts produced by Aider without validation
IF B then uploads or publishes those artifacts to external platforms
mitigations: Insert a human review step before upload
Compare Aider outputs against source-of-truth files
Restrict B to a staging account
Require checksum verification on artifacts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch source code/git history versus video, images, and account data, so no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. However, Aider’s model-provider API-key use and B’s account-data handling could create policy gaps if sensitive media or credentials are placed in the shared workflow. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair’s combined handling.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into the shared repo or prompts
IF the configured model provider or upload target has stricter retention than the operator expects
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider retention settings
Use test accounts for uploads
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive files
